plotSections.title: Keystone Assignments Completed
bullets: Ord formally accepts responsibility for protecting Feldspar and receives its keystone.
Plymouth finishes assigning the remaining keystones by explaining the responsibilities to Ciri.
Plymouth reiterates the party's individual assignments: Gerk protects Midgard, Sylan protects Gilbrick, Dana protects Pitel, Walker protects the Reach, Ord protects Feldspar, and Ciri chooses Lith.
Ciri chooses to become the keeper of Lith, completing the six player assignments while La-rel and Terov remain without mortal keepers.

plotSections.title: The Burden of the Keepers
bullets: Plymouth reminds the party that they originally began this journey with more companions and that the two unclaimed keystones should symbolize those who are no longer present.
La-rel and Terov will remain under the stewardship of Plymouth, Kit Anger, and the other children of the Great Eldarin Tree until worthy successors are found.
Plymouth emphasizes that they are only temporary stewards and intend to pass the keystones to future keepers when the time comes.
Plymouth warns that although the party sought to stop a lich, they now personally possess the artifacts the lich seeks, placing themselves in even greater danger.
The party is instructed to protect the keystones above all else, while Plymouth explains he cannot command how they use them but can only offer guidance.

plotSections.title: Children of the Great Eldarin Tree
bullets: Plymouth explains that by accepting the mantle of keystone keeper, each party member has become an honorary member of the Navi and a Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
Kit Anger welcomes the party as brothers and sisters of the tree, formally acknowledging their new status.

plotSections.title: The Doorman Revealed
bullets: Plymouth clarifies that Gerk is uniquely the 'Doorman,' while the rest of the party are Gatekeepers.
Following Plymouth's instructions, Gerk instinctively grasps an invisible door handle and successfully opens a doorway through reality.
The doorway reveals a beach somewhere in Midgard, demonstrating Gerk's innate ability to create portals despite Plymouth having little understanding of how the power functions.
Sylan attempts to replicate the feat using his keystone but only briefly senses something before failing, suggesting the ability requires greater mastery.
Plymouth admits he is relying on ancient records because no one has exercised these abilities for centuries.
